object_description: richly structured staggered two-story school building
design_condition: The staggered building closes the schoolyard toward the open space, creates an entrance area along the access path, and assigns the southern plot to enclosed outdoor space for the basic levels.

positive.statement: The staggered volume creates attractive spatial variety, including high rooms and skylights.

position.target: staggered volume with high rooms and skylights
position.rationale: Upper staggered masses and roof-level punctuations are visible in plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The volume establishes a subtle reference to the existing school's volumetrics.

position.rationale: The varied overall massing provides the available geometric reference for volumetric integration.

positive.statement: The organization of the room groups is positive.

position.rationale: Interior grouping is not directly legible, so the central occupied building zone anchors the judgment.

positive.statement: The corridor forms the backbone of the building, with daylight and views toward the schoolyard and playground.

position.rationale: A longitudinal internal route is approximated through the building’s central staggered spine.

positive.statement: Each basic level has separate access and direct exit to a spacious outdoor area.

position.target: separate basic-level access and outdoor exits
position.rationale: The southern edge visibly adjoins the enclosed outdoor area and likely ground-level exits.

positive.statement: The building is atmospheric and carefully integrated into the school complex.

position.rationale: The complete staggered envelope is the spatial basis for integration within the school complex.

positive.statement: Compliance with the primary energy and ecological requirements has been demonstrated.

position.rationale: This is a performance judgment without a useful spatial referent.

negative.statement: The planted island and spaced green on the north side are not convincing.

position.target: planted island and spaced green on north side
position.rationale: The northern perimeter provides the directional surface anchor for the questioned landscape.

negative.statement: It is unclear how students reach the sports fields.

position.rationale: Sports-field access is not identifiable; an external ground-level edge location is estimated.

negative.statement: Using the climate-buffer access area as a group and lounge room is probably not possible throughout the year.

position.rationale: The access condition is not distinguishable, so a low-level perimeter entry zone is approximated.

negative.statement: Mixing different age groups in the access area is problematic from an operational perspective.

position.rationale: The operationally shared access area is approximated at the same perimeter entry zone.

negative.statement: The accesses to the basic-school and day-school classrooms are narrow and awkward.

position.rationale: Classroom entrances are not individually visible; a lower side facade zone provides a constrained anchor.

negative.statement: The separate stairs make orientation difficult.

position.rationale: Stairs are not identifiable, so the central circulation zone is used as an approximate marker.

negative.statement: The energy concept is relatively complex, and individual measures would need to be questioned.

position.rationale: This operational complexity judgment has no useful spatial referent.

negative.statement: The accessibility of the adjoining design rooms has not been conclusively resolved.

position.rationale: Design rooms are not distinguishable; an adjoining lower side zone is estimated from the envelope.
